question: What platform guidance applies to handling the outcome of an AL HttpClient call that exports data to an external API, including transport failures, HTTP status codes and write transactions?
answer: Per microsoft/knowledge/web-services/handle-httpclient-platform-failure-before-response-access.md, if the optional Boolean return of Get, Post, Put, Delete or Send is captured and is false, stop processing the response and report or propagate the transport failure without reading status, headers or content; omitting the Boolean is also valid when fail-fast behavior is intended. Per microsoft/knowledge/web-services/check-http-status-before-consuming-response-body.md, a true result only means the exchange completed, so check IsSuccessStatusCode or the expected HttpStatusCode before treating the body as a success payload, and handle non-success status explicitly. Per microsoft/knowledge/performance/httpclient-inside-write-transaction-holds-locks.md, do not call HttpClient after writes in an open write transaction because locks stay held for the call duration; defer the call to a separate session, for example by inserting an outbox work item in the same transaction and processing committed outbox rows with a recurring job queue entry, and do not use Commit() as a general remedy. The retry policy and error-handling requirements were not supplied and are not answered here.
